key_insight: State Transport Routing (STR) improves short-horizon PV forecasting by blending a frozen model’s output with two recent-state trajectories, guided by forecast horizon.
engineering_relevance: STR is a lightweight, drop-in adapter that can boost neural PV forecasters without retraining the backbone or changing longer-horizon predictions.
method: Uses the latest measured PV power level to form two auxiliary trajectories: level-based and trend-based.
A horizon-conditioned router weights these trajectories during the first 120 minutes.
Leaves forecasts beyond 120 minutes unchanged, preserving the original long-horizon behavior.
evidence_signal: Across four public PV datasets, STR consistently beats a matched residual adapter; on PVDAQ it improves five neural backbones and lowers all-horizon NMAE by 0.0201–0.2364 percentage points with 95% confidence intervals excluding zero.
watch_item: The approach showed no reliable improvement for LightGBM, so gains may depend on the forecasting architecture.
paper_title: State Transport Routing for Short-horizon Adaptation in Multi-horizon Photovoltaic Forecasting
